title: Kernel Exposure Simulator and Entropy-Aware Prefill Scheduler
creator: Jordan Liu
description: Problem: Recent v3 kernel rollouts showed intermittent tail-latency spikes on multi-tenant hosts for mid-length contexts (128-1024) where the kernel selector oscillates during prefill->decode handoff. Goal: build a simulator to quantify kernel exposure windows and a runtime scheduling policy that uses token-level entropy predictions to choose microbatch tiling and prefilling aggressiveness per-request. Deliverables: 1) a deterministic Kernel Exposure Simulator (KES) that replays production traces and models v2/v3 kernel choice, memory fragmentation, and warmup cost; 2) an entropy predictor that runs on prefix tokens and produces a 3-tier confidence score used by the Prefill Scheduler; 3) a staged canary + rollback plan with telemetry-driven thresholds and mitigations. Success criteria: reduce 95th percentile decode latency delta between v2 and v3 rollouts by >= 20% on affected shapes without increasing mean GPU token-cost by >5%.
comments: 2025-11-04 — Kickoff: scoped KES prototype. Decided to model kernel warmup cost as 'cold kernel activation time' + 'inflight workspace compaction penalty' instead of purely measuring workspace allocation to capture fragmentation effects.

2025-11-06 — Data pull: exported 72 hours of production request traces (tenant anonymized IDs). Sampled 50k traces with contexts 64-1024, tagged by model family and quantization profile. Stored replay set ref: gs://redwood-prod-traces/entropy-prefill/2025-11-06-sample.jsonl.

2025-11-09 — Prototype KES run (single-GPU simulated): observed two primary failure modes: (A) v3 kernel selection flip during long prefill bursts causing extra workspace reallocation; (B) small-batch decode steps selecting a v2 path with higher per-token latency due to head-slicing interaction. Attached dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/KES/entropy-prefill-sim-20251109.

2025-11-11 — Design decision: use an entropy heuristic (prefix token surprisal aggregated via lightweight 1-layer LM) to predict branching probability; map predicted classes to prefill aggressiveness: HIGH => coalesce into larger microbatches and enable optimistic v3 warmup; MEDIUM => conservative tiling with KV-preserve mode; LOW => prefer v2 stable kernels to minimize fragmentation.

2025-11-13 — Engineering note: implemented KES toggles for workspace-reuse strategies and a synthetic fragmentation noise generator to test worst-case host-level allocation churn. KES repo branch: github.com/redwood/inference/kes/feature/entropy-prefill.

2025-11-15 — Benchmarks: run KES replay on sampled traces comparing baseline selector vs entropy-scheduler. Results: 95p decode latency down 27% on shape bucket 256-512; mean token GPU time increased 3.1% (within tolerance). Observed a small regression in tail memory spills on mixed-tenant hosts when optimistic v3 warmup enabled for too many concurrent tenants.

2025-11-16 — Review feedback from SRE (Marta Kovács): require additional safety net — per-host concurrency cap for optimistic warmup and a backoff window when memory spill rate > 0.5% over 1 minute. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-11-18 — Security/Compliance note: no customer data surfaced; entropy predictor runs only on token IDs and local LM embeddings; still flagged for optional audit during private deployments. Marked security_review_required=false for hosted rollout, but add security checklist for Private.

2025-11-19 — Canary plan drafted: 1) internal canary on Dedicated pool dev-2 (10% traffic), monitor 95p decode latency, work-alloc-failure, and OOM signals; 2) customer beta (handful of tenants) with opt-in; rollback triggers: any 95p decode latency regression > +10% or memory spill > 1% for 5 minutes.

2025-11-20 — Blocker logged: observed intermittent false-positive HIGH entropy classifications for code-completion workloads due to prefix tokens being syntactic. Mitigation: add a simple token-type classifier to downscale entropy score for code-like prefixes; follow-up spike: ENG-890124.

Next steps: (1) finalize KES edge-case modeling and run 7-day replay to validate stability; (2) implement per-host warmup cap and backoff in runtime scheduler; (3) open PRs for entropy predictor + scheduler (target PR creation 2025-11-22); (4) schedule SRE + PM sync for canary kickoff 2025-11-25.
